title: kv-cache zero-copy dequantor + per-layer scale for hybrid INT8/FP8 paths
author: Maya Chen
commits: init: add zero-copy staging buffers and API hooks for KV uploads
perf: implement per-layer scale table and runtime selection for dequant path
kernel: add fused dequant+copy microkernel (int8 -> fp16) with alignment fallback
scheduler: KV-aware continuous batching affinity and zero-copy fastpath
tests: unit + microbench harness for per-layer scale selection and correctness
docs: runtime notes and rollout checklist
body:
Summary: This PR introduces a KV-cache-aware zero-copy dequantor to bridge INT8/FP8 model weights with the FP16 execution path without an explicit full-buffer dequant allocation. It also adds a per-layer scale table and runtime selection policy to reduce quantization overhead and variance for mixed INT8/FP8 model variants.

Motivation: we saw two related issues in production benches: (1) dequant buffer allocations and copies dominated short inference tails for small requests under continuous batching, and (2) a single global scale for requant/dequant caused output quality variability across certain layers (particularly large-attention heads). The goal is to reduce latency/cost and reduce quality regressions when switching to INT8/FP8 hybrid paths.

Design:
- Zero-copy KV staging: when loading KV blocks for attention, the runtime now exposes an optional staging pointer that the dequant microkernel can write into directly while applying dequant scaling. For compatible devices/drivers this avoids a separate host/device memcpy.
- Per-layer scale table: a compact table stored alongside model metadata with per-layer requant/dequant multipliers and a small 8-bit exponent adjustment. The runtime chooses the appropriate multiplier at serving time based on model variant and input distribution (simple moving avg statistics).
- Fused microkernel: implemented an aligned-fallback microkernel that performs int8 -> fp16 dequant + layout transpose when needed. It uses packed vector instructions and falls back to a scalar path for tails.
- Scheduler integration: continuous-batcher now marks KV-preload requests with a 'zero_copy_capable' flag and preferentially routes them to nodes with pinned memory regions, enabling the fastpath while preserving fairness.
- Safety and correctness: added runtime checks for alignment, driver support, and a graceful fallback to the previous dequant path if zero-copy is unavailable.

Checklist:
- [x] Microkernel implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Runtime hooks and API flags
- [x] Continuous batching affinity integration
- [x] Bench harness and end-to-end latency/throughput tests
- [x] Docs and rollout plan
- [x] Canary configuration for Dedicated clusters

Performance results (internal bench):
- Model: open-counter-XL (seq_len 128, batch sizes 1..16)
- Baseline (int8 dequant -> copy -> fp16 exec): median p95 tail 9.8ms, throughput @64 tokens/s
- New fastpath: median p95 tail 7.1ms (-27.6% tail), throughput @77 tokens/s (+20%)
- Memory: peak temporary dequant buffer reduced by ~34% on average
- Cost estimate: token compute cost down ~12% due to reduced memcpy and more efficient kernel util.

Reproducibility: microbench harness included in tests/runtime/bench/kv_zero_copy_bench.py; CI runs the smoke variant and benchlab has extended runs under perf-canary.

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/kv/staging.h (new API)
- runtime/kv/staging.cc (implementation + fallbacks)
- runtime/dequant/microkernel_int8_to_fp16.S (optimized kernel)
- runtime/dequant/dequant_table.{h,cc} (per-layer scale table and loader)
- runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cc (affinity + flag plumbing)
- runtime/tests/test_dequant_table.py (unit tests)
- runtime/tests/bench/kv_zero_copy_bench.py (bench harness)
- docs/runtime/quantization.md (rollout notes and config)
- examples/bench/ci-cfg.yaml (CI bench trigger)

Small illustrative snippet (pseudocode in one line): "if (zero_copy_capable && align_ok) dequant_kernel_zero_copy(src_int8, dst_kv_staging_ptr, scale) else dequant_to_temp_and_copy(...)"

Review thread summary:
- Arjun: requested a stronger guard around driver capabilities and suggested exposing an opt-in feature flag for Dedicated customers; author responded and added runtime flag config and a telemetry metric (runtime.zero_copy_used) (resolved).
- Sofia: asked for formal verification that numerical parity is within tolerance; author added unit tests that compare fp32 reference outputs and included a small per-layer calibration run; noted differences < 0.3% L2 for quantized layers (resolved).
- Liam: requested microbenchmark numbers on varied sequence lengths and a long-tail test; author added bench outputs and CI bench job link (resolved).

CI:
- Unit tests + linters + microbench smoke all passed in CI run #4217.
- Perf-canary runs on two Dedicated clusters show stable tails; one rewarmed node flagged driver alignment issue (runtime fell back; no errors).

Rollout plan:
Stage 1: merge to main, feature disabled by default.
Stage 2: enable opt-in on Dedicated internal canary (ENG-3421).
Stage 3: compare quality metrics for 48h; if stable, enable auto-selection for Hosted API on variant models supporting zero-copy.

Release notes:
- Added KV zero-copy dequant fastpath and per-layer scale table to reduce dequant allocations and improve throughput/tail latency.
- Feature gated and opt-in for Dedicated canary; safe fallback when unsupported.

Known limitations and follow-ups:
- Zero-copy relies on driver/allocator features; we added telemetry to capture fallbacks but still need broader matrix testing across GPU types (TODO: ENG-3499).
- Per-layer scale table currently uses simple moving average; a future PR will add an offline calibration tool to compute better layer-wise multipliers.

Related PRs and work items: ENG-3208 (quant rollout checklist), perf-canary jobs in perf-canary repo, and an internal note on mixed INT8/FP8 model idiosyncrasies.

Merge notes: squashed and merged; merged commit message includes perf numbers and the canary enablement flag commented out by default.
release_notes: KV zero-copy dequant fastpath: reduces temporary buffers and tail latency
Per-layer scale table: reduces quantization variance across large attention layers
Feature is gated; opt-in Dedicated canary before broader rollout
